## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ucchiṭṭhabhattajātaka* (Ja 212), translated in English as *A Meal of Leavings*, is a canonical narrative in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. In the standard edition of the *Jātaka* together with its commentary by V. Fausböll, it occurs in the second volume, placed between the *Somadattajātaka* and the *Bharujātaka* [Fausböll 1879].
The story is set while the Buddha was residing at Jetavana and was delivered regarding a monk who had grown lovesick and longed for his former wife (*purāṇadutiyikā*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The Buddha questioned the monk about his distress and revealed that in a former existence, the same woman had mistreated him by feeding him the leavings of food from her secret paramour [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The opening verse cited in the commentary begins with the line *Añño uparimo vaṇṇo* [Fausböll 1879]. At the conclusion of the past narrative (*samodhāna*), the Buddha revealed that the lovesick monk had been the deceived husband, the former wife had been the unfaithful woman, and the Bodhisatta had been the actor's son (*naṭaputta*) who uncovered the misdeed; upon the declaration of the four noble truths, the lovesick monk attained stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
SuttaCentral lists four modern translations across four languages but records no curated cross-language parallels [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus likewise finds no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above; Pali-internally, DharmaNexus records four matching passages between the canonical verses and the commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo), with the longest match spanning segments 2.1–2.4 [DharmaNexus].
